description: Create a visual interface showcasing a 2D/3D map of the Moon and Mars with areas of significance highlighted with markers. Clicking a marker shows location information: numeric factors (water ice, temperature fluctuations, solar energy, ease of mobility and landing) and listed factors (surface characteristic, surface materials, geological age). Data pulled from NASA databases to assign up to 5 Earth analogs with selection reasons, and mismatches.
summary:
I developed a website which gives you a 2D map of the Moon and Mars with potential future base sites marked. Once a site is selected you will get all available evidence for a base I gather from the various NASA and scientific sources. This data is then used to get up to 5 Earth analogs for each mission purpose (rover terrain and navigation, ice prospecting or excavation, thermal exposure testing, geological sampling, or power-system field testing). Using the data about a site, and the mission purpose listed by a user, this website can provide you with a prompt for your AI Agent containing all relevant data for your mission.
Only a limited number of base sites are available for now, but the focus was on perfecting each site so future expansion can be done easily
PATH addresses the challenging by not just providing accurate (scoured as many databases as possible and matched future base parameters with sites on Earth) Earth analogs, but also including features to better understand that data for simpler mission planning
details:
It works by using existing data from various NASA sources, and having various parameters ready to be filled with said data. This streamlines the process since all base loactions/sites will have the same set of parameters so it will be easier to compare.

Benefits include being able to visually identify the locations and find all the information you need about them in a single click. Analogs are provided for specific mission types not just "bases" in general. Additionally, for every landing site and mission purpose, the website can provide you with a zip file containing all the context you need to give to an AI Model for further work on the user side.

Intended impact is to make the process of testing for moon/mars base locations faster, and more streamlined without sacrificing accuracy.

Tools used

  • Frontend — HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript for the interactive maps and site explorer.
  • Backend and database — Python, Flask, and SQLite/SQL. Python’s zipfile library generates the evidence packages.
  • Geospatial processing — NumPy, Rasterio with GDAL, and pyproj with PROJ for elevation data, slope calculations, and coordinate transformations.
  • Development, testing, and hosting — Git and GitHub, Windows PowerShell, Python’s unittest, Node.js’s built-in test runner, and Vercel.
  • Scientific data and imagery — NASA’s Planetary Data System, Planetary Geodesy Data Archive, Earthdata, and POWER API, plus the USGS terrestrial analog catalog, the Polar Geospatial Center, the National Snow and Ice Data Center, and the Mars Climate Database. The basemaps use NASA Blue Marble, LROC lunar imagery, and NASA/JPL–USGS Viking imagery.

Project is creative because it starts off simple, selecting parameters for each site, but it makes sure to keep those parameters as detailed as possible all the while making comparison with Earth Analogs possible. Features like "Ask an Agent" also make it suited for use by even people without a technical background.

Main factors considered were accuracy, ease of use, detail, and visual appeal
